From: EdgeBank Security <security@edgebank.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial RFI: request for attack-lattice and control-plane separation evidence

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the fast responses so far. As part of our procurement security questionnaire for Redwood Inference we need:

1) A high-level network topology diagram showing tenant demarcation, control-plane vs data-plane boundaries, and egress choke points.
2) An annotated attack-lattice (threat tree) that shows plausible lateral movement paths and the mitigations you rely on for each hop.
3) Evidence artifacts for control-plane isolation (audit logs, role/permission model summary, and any attestation you can share).

We'd appreciate a single consolidated packet if possible. Auditor expects diagrams + an appendix with logs/evidence within 7 business days. Please confirm scope and any clarifying questions.

Regards,
Priya Sharma
Lead, Infrastructure Security
EdgeBank
[Attachment: edgebank_questionnaire_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Priya Sharma <security@edgebank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial RFI: request for attack-lattice and control-plane separation evidence

Priya — thanks for the clear ask. We're assembling a combined packet. Quick clarifications before we finalize:

- Do you need low-level Flow Logs (full packet captures) or summarized egress allowlist evidence? We typically provide summarized flow tables and sampled audit traces for compliance packets.
- For attestation: are you accepting vendor-signed audit summaries + RBAC exports, or do you require dedicated HSM-backed signed attestations?

What we'll provide in the packet (deliverable list):
- redwood_network_diagram_v3.png — annotated topology (control-plane, data-plane, tenant overlay, sidecar proxies, egress chokepoints)
- attack-tree-edgebank-v1.pdf — threat-lattice with hypothesis, likelihood, and control mapping
- controlplane-dataplane-evidence.csv — RBAC snapshot + recent control-plane audit events (redacted)
- Appendix: sampling of traceroutes and connection allowlist exports (sanitized)

I've attached a preview of the topology and the threat-lattice. Kimberly will help with the RBAC export and the audit excerpts; Marissa will coordinate the packaging for the auditor. We'll push the final Drive packet and a signed cover note by Friday (2026-06-19).

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_network_diagram_v3.png (image/png); Attachment: attack-tree-edgebank-v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: EdgeBank RFI — packaging notes and redaction checklist

Sergio / Kimberly — forwarding Priya's RFI thread. Notes for packaging the evidence packet: 

- Redaction checklist: remove IP-level identifiers for unrelated tenants, redact account IDs except for sample audit lines that show control-plane actions tied to service-account foo-redwood-ops.
- RBAC export format: CSV with columns {principal, role, scope, last_activity} — include hashed principal IDs and a legend mapping hashed id -> role for auditor use only.
- Audit events: include the last 90 days of control-plane role grants and the last 30 days of model-pinning/rollout operations. Provide one signed excerpt from our internal logging pipeline (we can add a PGP/GPG signature).
- Threat lattice: add a row describing 'cache poisoning via shared KV' and include the mitigation (prefix isolation + per-tenant KV namespaces + signed cache metadata).

Kimberly — can you produce the RBAC CSV + signature by EOD Wednesday? I'll curate the diagrams and assemble the Drive link.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Priya Sharma <security@edgebank.com>, Auditor Team <auditor@thirdparty-audit.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Delivered: EdgeBank evidence packet — topology, attack lattice, and control-plane artifacts

Priya / EdgeBank Audit Team —

Attached is the final evidence packet and Drive bundle. Summary highlights below; full artifacts are in the shared Drive link. If you want an encrypted tranche (PGP) for the RBAC export we can provide that separately.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Control-plane vs Data-plane: Redwood enforces logical demarcation via a separate control-plane fleet with mutual TLS and strict mTLS client certificates. Control-plane operations that change routing, model pinning, or tenant assignments occur only through the control-plane and require RBAC-signed tokens.
- Tenant isolation: Each tenant is scoped to a per-tenant namespace for KV cache, ephemeral model KV caches, and storage buckets; overlay networking prevents cross-tenant L4 connectivity in the data-plane. Sidecar proxies enforce per-request principal binding and strip any inbound egress requests that violate allowlists.
- Egress controls: Central egress gateways (regional) implement outbound allowlists; we provide sampled allowlist exports and proxy deny-rate metrics.
- Threat lattice: We included an annotated attack tree focused on (a) operator credential compromise, (b) sidecar escape and KV poisoning, (c) control-plane API misuse. For each node we show detection signals (audit events, telemetry signatures) and containment playbooks.

Included artifacts (Drive links and attached files):
- redwood_network_diagram_v3.png — annotated network topology and trusted demarcations
- attack-tree-edgebank-v1.pdf — full threat lattice with mitigations and detection controls
- controlplane-dataplane-evidence.csv — RBAC export + sample signed audit lines (redacted)
- Appendix: allowlist-sample.csv, proxy-deny-metrics-30d.csv, signed-audit-excerpt.asc

Notes / constraints:
- We redacted tenant-specific IPs unrelated to EdgeBank. The RBAC export uses hashed principal IDs and includes a legend for the auditor under separate transfer (DocuSign + secure Drive).
- Full flow logs and raw packet captures are not provided by default; we can arrange additional retention snapshots under an LOA if EdgeBank needs them for forensics.

Next steps: please confirm receipt and whether the auditor wants a short walkthrough call. We can schedule a 30-minute evidence walkthrough (we recommend Sergio + Kimberly + one of our engineers).

Thanks — looking forward to your feedback.

Sergio Alvarez
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
